newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New Year date change halts Brussels stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: New Year date change halts Brussels stock exchange.

text.p: The Brussels Stock Exchange got an advance preview Thursday of the so-called Millennium problem -- in which some computer programmes may be unable to recognise the year 2000.
The exchange's trading system crashed due to the New Year date change and trading was halted for three hours until the problem could be fixed.
"There is a technical problem with the change of date which is causing problems in one programme," market director Olivier Lefebvre said when the market failed to open.
Lefebvre said one of the problems was that orders that were placed on Dec. 30, the last trading day of 1996, were being recognised as December 1997 orders.

This prevented investors and brokerages from changing their orders to reflect Wall Street's plunge Tuesday, when the Dow Jones industrial average lost 101.10 points to 6,448.27, leaving it up 26 percent for the year after a rise of 33.5 percent in 1995.
The Belgian market was closed Tuesday and Wednesday for an extended New Year break.
The computer glitch was the most serious technical problem to hit the Brussels market since a new trading system was installed last year.
